full_judgment:
Ruhul Islam. J.-This appeal by special leave arises out of the judgment dated November 30, 1976 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court in Criminal Revision case No. 559 of 1975. 

 2. Facts in short are that one Abdul Quader lodged First Information Report in the Chhatak police station alleging that on 25.9.73 at about 12-45 hours an armed dacoity was committed in his house. The dacoits killed his cousin brother Abdul Karim and assaulted and injured the complainant, and his lather Aftab Ali. The dacoits were armed with rifle, "dao", and 'lathis'. They took away various articles from the house worth Tk. 11,370/00. The complainant and the other inmates recognized six of the dacoits but other 12/15 dacoits could not be recognised. It was further alleged that hearing the gun shots, the villagers came and heard about the occurrence. The police started investigation and G.R. case No. 552 of 1973 was initiated in the Court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sunamganj, Sylhet, The Officer-in-Charge of Chhatak Police Station submitted a report to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate with a prayer for issuing processes against the appellants and others. The appellant Charag Ali was named as witness No. 1 in the First Information Report, by an order dated 8.11.73 the Sub-Divisional Magistrate issued W/A and P/A against the appellants and other co-accused as prayed for. The Police after investigation submitted charged sheet on 7.9.74 against some of the accused under section 396 of the Bangladesh Penal Code read with President's Order No. 50 or 1972 and submitted final report against the appellants and 36 others, as the case was not proved against them and prayed for recalling the warrants. The Magistrate by his order of the same date discharged the accused not charge-sheeted and recalled the warrants as recommended by the Police. Thereafter the complainant filed a 'narajee' petition on 27.1.75 alleging bias of the Police and prayed for issue of process against the appellants and other three co-accused. On perusal of the police report and other records Mr. F. Karim, the Magistrate First Class passed the following order on the same date: 

 4. Against this order the appellants moved the Sessions Judge, Sylhet under Section 438/ 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was rejected on 31.7.75. They moved the High Court in the revisional jurisdiction and Rule was issued in Revisional Case No. 559 of 1975 which was discharged on 3.11.76. Against that judgment the appellants obtained leave from this Court. Leave was granted to examine the question whether the Magistrate was competent to take cognizance of the. Offence on information other than a report of a Police Officer in terms of article 4(i) and 1 (A) of P.O. 50 of 1972. 

 4. Mr. Kamaluddin Ahmed, Advocate appearing for the complainant respondent submitted that P.O. 50 of 1972 was repealed on 9.2.74 and the charge sheet was Submitted after the said repeal on 7.9.74 and as such the case ceased to be a case under the special statute but continued to be a case under the ordinary criminal law and as such an illegality has been committed by the Magistrate in this case in issuing warrants on consideration of the report of the Police submitted under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the 'narajee' filed by the complainant ever, does not support such argument. The Magistrate by his order dated 27.2.75 issued warrants against the appellant and 5 others under section 396 of the Bangladesh Penal Code read with P.O. 50 of 1972. The case against the charge sheeted accused was also pending under section 396 of the Penal Code read with P.O. 50, of 1972. Therefore, it is difficult to accept the submission of the learned Advocate that the case on 'narajee' filed by the complainant was proceeding as an ordinary criminal case after the 'narajee' petition was entertained, in view of the repeal of PO 50 of 1972. The learned Judges of the High Court Division were not correct in basing their decision on the assumption that the case against the appellant anti 5 others on revival on the 'narajee' was proceeding as an ordinary case under the Penal Code. 

 5. Mr. Shawkat Ali Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, however, submitted that order-sheet of the case would clearly show that the case was continuing as one under the special statute, namely, PO. 50 of 1972, and not as an ordinary criminal case under the Penal Code. He submitted that the learned Judge of the High Court Division did nor correctly appreciate the facts of the case and accordingly, discharged the Rule on the erroneous view that The submission of final report so far as the accused petitioner is concerned has not created right inhering in him so as to dis-entitle the prosecution to prosecute with evidence which was not available earlier". He further submitted that this case, in any view of the matter, is fully covered by the decisions of this Court namely, (1) Akhtar Hossain Khan and ors. Vs. State, 29 D.L.R. (S C.) 101 and (2) Abdur Rahman versus-State, 29 D.L.R. (S.C.) 256. On the authority of 29 D.L.R (S.C.) 101 the learned Counsel added that P.O. 50 of 1972 was correctly mentioned in the impugned order of the Magistrate dated 27.2.75, because, the case being a pending one it was not affected by the repeal of P.O. 50 of 1972. The learned Counsel contended that the order of discharge being a judicial order It could not be superseded by a subsequent order passed by the learned Magistrate, and as such he acted illegally in issuing warrants against the appellant and 5 others already discharged and this amounted to taking cognizance of the offence against the appellant and S others an entertaining 'narajee' filed by the complainant. According to him the contention is fortified by the decision reported in 29 D.L.R. (SC) 256. He also referred to a decision of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Abul Hossain Sana Vs. Sawalal Agarwala, (1962) 14 D.L.R. (S.C.) 96 P.L.D. 1952 (SC) 242, wherein it has been held that once an order of discharge has been recorded by the Magistrate revival of proceedings is not permitted in the absence of an order of the Revisional Court revising the same. 

 6. On perusal of the record of the case it appears that appellant Cherag Ali was cited as a witness in the First Information Report, but after carrying on investigation against him along with others also not named as accused in the first Information Report, with permission from the Court. final report was submitted against them. On perusal of the report and other relevant papers the Magistrate discharged them from the case on September 7, 1974 and recalled the processes. Subsequently, on February 27, 1975 the complainant filed a 'narajee' petition, upon which the Magistrate passed the impugned order directing issue of warrants of arrest. 

 7. From the judgment of the Sessions Judge and that of the High Court Division in revision it appears that one important aspect of the case has been totally missed, Since the case was initiated under the special statute and it was so continuing the Magistrate was not competent to discharge the accused on the basis of the report of the Police. The offence being exclusively triable by the Special Tribunal, it was for the Special Tribunal to decide whether on the basis of the police report cognizance should be taken or not. The Magistrate acted without jurisdiction in discharging the accused not charge-sheeted. Proper course would be to send the report along with the record to the Special Tribunal for passing the necessary orders. However, the learned Magistrate after hearing the prosecution on February 27, 1975 issued warrants against the appellant and 5 others. This order cannot be said to be an order taking cognizance of the offence against the appellant and others. The argument advanced at the Bar in this respect are misconceived. The case being triable under the special statute, that is, P.O. 50 of 1972 the decision in the matter lies with the Special Tribunal. It is for the Special Tribunal to decide whether there are materials for taking cognizance of the offence alleged against the accused. The learned Magistrate should have sent the record of the case to the Special Tribunal for necessary orders. 

 8. The learned Judges of the High Court while observing that "submission of final report against the accused does not create any right inhering in him so as to disentitle the prosecution to prosecute with the evidence which was not available earlier, did not properly appreciate the facts of this case. This led to the erroneous view taken by the learned Judges that the Magistrate validly passed the impugned order. This also amounts to approving the earlier order of the Magistrate discharging the accused not charge-sheeted. The case reported in 14 D.L.R. (SC) 96 which has been followed in the case reported in 29 D.L.R.(SC), 256 has no application to the facts of this case. 

 In that view of the matter the order of the Magistrate dated February 27, 1975 cannot be sustained. In the result the appeal is allowed, the order of the High Court is set aside and the order of the Magistrate dated February 27, 1975 is quashed. The case should proceed in accordance with law and the observations made above.
